doc_summary: the open screen hears of a key press (`native_screen_key_pressed_pre`) and of each character it types (`native_screen_char_typed_pre`) before it acts, as vanilla's `ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Pre` and `.CharacterTyped.Pre`: the screen, vanilla's key name (`key.keyboard.e`, as `native_key` hands it over; a key with no name fires nothing), whether the press is an auto-repeat, the character, GLFW's modifier bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8), and `screen.mouse` for the pointer. A cancelled press goes no further — no focus move, no Escape-close, no inventory or hotbar key, no text box, no `native_key` — while its release still arrives, so a `native_key` listener sees that release without its press. A cancelled character drops only that character and never reaches a text box; the characters fire even when the press was cancelled, as vanilla delivers `charTyped` anyway, and control characters (Enter, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Escape, a Control letter) are keys and fire nothing. The input method's committed text fires the character hook too. They fire on the window only, after the fullscreen, screenshot, debug and narrator keys, never on the title screen itself (Options and the pack list opened from it do fire), the connect and loading screens, the prompts, books and sign editors drawn over gameplay, or while a world loads or saves. Bundles need "hooks": @API:screen_key_input@.
